chunks: ʿAlī, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Regarding a man who kills his owned slave deliberately, he said:
“It is pleasing to me that he should free a slave, fast two consecutive months, and feed sixty needy persons; then repentance would be after that.”

key_terms.رَقَبَةً: a slave to be set free as expiation
key_terms.سِتِّينَ مِسْكِينًا: sixty needy persons to be fed

ai.seo_question: What expiation is mentioned in Tahdhib al-Ahkam for a man who deliberately kills his slave?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal-ethical response concerning one who deliberately kills his slave. It mentions expiatory acts—freeing a slave, fasting two consecutive months, and feeding sixty needy persons—followed by tawbah, showing the gravity of the act and the path of return.
